classification_basis: DSM-5-TR-oriented MDD module; no silent ICD-11 criteria merge

clinical_review.scope: Adult MDD assessment and provisional explanation for professional review; not prescribing or autonomous diagnosis.

frequency_qualifiers.mood_interest: Most of day, nearly daily; breadth matters for interest/pleasure.
frequency_qualifiers.other_daily_domains: Nearly daily applies to appetite, sleep, motor, energy, guilt/worthlessness and cognition formulations.
frequency_qualifiers.exceptions: Weight has its own change/time formulation; death/suicide reports have distinct recurrent/plan/attempt formulations. Do not impose daily occurrence on all.
frequency_qualifiers.weight_example: More than 5% body-weight change over a month is a source example, not a rule for all complaints.

disorder_boundaries.meaning: Review physiological substance/medical explanations; no causal conclusion from timing alone.
At least one qualifying episode must satisfy the current psychotic-disorder exclusion.
Review lifetime mania/hypomania; preserve substance/medical exceptions and treatment context for professional interpretation.

course_review.recurrence: Separate episodes require at least two consecutive months without full MDE criteria between them; not necessarily total symptom freedom.
course_review.partial_remission: Residual symptoms without full criteria, or less than two months without significant symptoms after an episode.
course_review.full_remission: At least two months without significant signs/symptoms.
course_review.severity: Symptoms, intensity and functioning together; mild/moderate/severe cannot be inferred from one symptom or an informal count.
course_review.label_application: Current severity/psychotic coding and remission coding apply under different current-episode conditions; no billing codes are generated.

clinical_review.safety: Directly assess ideation/intent and immediate needs; use dedicated professional pathway rather than a predicted low/medium/high score.

concepts.label: Depressed mood
concepts.definition: Reported low, sad or empty mood.

description.meaning: The person's account of this experience, without adding a diagnosis.

onset.meaning: When this particular experience began; preserve approximate wording.

duration.meaning: How long this particular experience has continued, not time needed to perform an activity.

frequency.meaning: Reported recurrence within an explicit reference period; no invented numeric conversion.

days_per_week.meaning: Stated days affected; keep units and wording instead of imposing a diagnostic cutoff.

proportion_of_day.meaning: Reported share of an affected day; most of the day is already useful.

baseline_comparison.meaning: How this differs from the person's usual state.

impact.meaning: Concrete reported consequences of this experience.

concepts.question_example: How has your mood been during this period?
concepts.followup_focus: Meaning, persistence and episode timing if unclear.
concepts.do_not_infer: A sad day alone does not establish the domain threshold or MDD.
concepts.criterion_review_note: Review most-of-day and near-daily persistence within the shared episode period.

concepts.label: Interest and pleasure
concepts.definition: Reduced desire for activities and/or reduced enjoyment.

onset.meaning: When this particular experience began; preserve approximate wording.

duration.meaning: How long this particular experience has continued, not time needed to perform an activity.

frequency.meaning: Reported recurrence within an explicit reference period; no invented numeric conversion.

days_per_week.meaning: Stated days affected; keep units and wording instead of imposing a diagnostic cutoff.

proportion_of_day.meaning: Reported share of an affected day; most of the day is already useful.

interest.meaning: Reported wanting or motivation to engage.

baseline_comparison.meaning: How this differs from the person's usual state.

concepts.question_example: Have your interest or enjoyment in your usual activities changed?
concepts.followup_focus: Separate wanting from enjoying; establish breadth if relevant.
concepts.do_not_infer: One retained hobby does not negate all symptoms; not doing an activity may reflect lack of opportunity.
concepts.criterion_review_note: The clinical criterion concerns a marked reduction across all or almost all activities, most of the day, nearly daily; one affected hobby alone is insufficient.

concepts.label: Appetite change
concepts.definition: Change in desire for food.

onset.meaning: When this particular experience began; preserve approximate wording.

duration.meaning: How long this particular experience has continued, not time needed to perform an activity.

frequency.meaning: Reported recurrence within an explicit reference period; no invented numeric conversion.

baseline_comparison.meaning: How this differs from the person's usual state.

impact.meaning: Concrete reported consequences of this experience.

concepts.question_example: Has your appetite changed compared with usual?
concepts.followup_focus: Direction, persistence and appetite versus eating.
concepts.do_not_infer: Do not invent weight change from appetite; shares one count group with weight.
concepts.criterion_review_note: Appetite increase/decrease has a near-daily qualifier; actual intake is not interchangeable with appetite.

concepts.label: Weight change
concepts.definition: Reported change in body weight.

amount.meaning: Amount with original units; no guessing.

concepts.question_example: Have you noticed a change in your weight during this period?
concepts.followup_focus: Amount, interval and intentionality when relevant.
concepts.do_not_infer: No automatic percent calculation without compatible stated weights and dates; never double-count appetite.
concepts.criterion_review_note: Significant non-dieting weight change has its own amount/time formulation; an amount alone without interval cannot establish it.

concepts.label: Sleep disturbance
concepts.definition: Difficulty sleeping or excessive sleep.

onset.meaning: When this particular experience began; preserve approximate wording.

duration.meaning: How long this particular experience has continued, not time needed to perform an activity.

frequency.meaning: Reported recurrence within an explicit reference period; no invented numeric conversion.

baseline_comparison.meaning: How this differs from the person's usual state.

awakenings.meaning: Waking during sleep and return-to-sleep account.

daytime_effect.meaning: Sleepiness, exhaustion or other reported effects.

concepts.question_example: How has your sleep changed from what is usual for you?
concepts.followup_focus: Identify complaint before asking subtype-specific details.
concepts.do_not_infer: Insomnia while tired is not reduced sleep need; insufficient opportunity is not automatically insomnia.
concepts.criterion_review_note: Review near-daily insomnia/hypersomnia rather than assuming all short sleep is insomnia.

concepts.label: Psychomotor change
concepts.definition: Noticeable motor/speech slowing or agitation.

onset.meaning: When this particular experience began; preserve approximate wording.

frequency.meaning: Reported recurrence within an explicit reference period; no invented numeric conversion.

observer.meaning: Who noticed it; self-report about another observer remains patient report.

baseline_comparison.meaning: How this differs from the person's usual state.

impact.meaning: Concrete reported consequences of this experience.

concepts.question_example: Have you or other people noticed changes in how quickly you move or speak?
concepts.followup_focus: Observable examples and reporter, rather than restlessness alone.
concepts.do_not_infer: Text response speed and feeling restless alone do not establish observable psychomotor change.
concepts.criterion_review_note: Requires observable agitation/slowing, not solely a subjective sense of restlessness/slowness.

concepts.label: Energy and fatigue
concepts.definition: Unusual tiredness or reduced energy.

onset.meaning: When this particular experience began; preserve approximate wording.

duration.meaning: How long this particular experience has continued, not time needed to perform an activity.

frequency.meaning: Reported recurrence within an explicit reference period; no invented numeric conversion.

baseline_comparison.meaning: How this differs from the person's usual state.

impact.meaning: Concrete reported consequences of this experience.

concepts.question_example: How has your energy been compared with usual?
concepts.followup_focus: Examples and timing; separate sleepiness if ambiguous.
concepts.do_not_infer: Do not automatically attribute fatigue to depression or infer it from short sleep.
concepts.criterion_review_note: Review near-daily fatigue/loss of energy; cause still requires contextual assessment.

concepts.label: Worthlessness and guilt
concepts.definition: Low self-worth or excessive/inappropriate guilt.

onset.meaning: When this particular experience began; preserve approximate wording.

duration.meaning: How long this particular experience has continued, not time needed to perform an activity.

frequency.meaning: Reported recurrence within an explicit reference period; no invented numeric conversion.

kind.meaning: Which experience is actually reported: feeling worthless, guilt, both, or unclear. This label does not by itself establish excessive/inappropriate guilt or its diagnostic threshold.

context.meaning: What the thought concerns; retain uncertainty about proportionality.

impact.meaning: Concrete reported consequences of this experience.

concepts.question_example: How have you been thinking about yourself during this period?
concepts.followup_focus: Actual thought content; clarify without endorsing it.
concepts.do_not_infer: Ordinary regret, low confidence and guilt about illness are not automatically qualifying guilt.
concepts.criterion_review_note: Review near-daily worthlessness or excessive/inappropriate guilt; illness-related self-reproach alone is insufficient.

concepts.label: Concentration and decisions
concepts.definition: Reported thinking, attention or decision difficulty.

onset.meaning: When this particular experience began; preserve approximate wording.

duration.meaning: How long this particular experience has continued, not time needed to perform an activity.

frequency.meaning: Reported recurrence within an explicit reference period; no invented numeric conversion.

baseline_comparison.meaning: How this differs from the person's usual state.

impact.meaning: Concrete reported consequences of this experience.

concepts.question_example: Have concentrating or making decisions become harder than usual?
concepts.followup_focus: Task examples and change from baseline.
concepts.do_not_infer: Do not label dementia, ADHD or depression from this alone.
concepts.criterion_review_note: Review near-daily thinking/concentration/decision difficulty and change from baseline.

concepts.label: Death/suicide-related reports
concepts.definition: Death-related thoughts, suicidal thoughts, plans or attempts.

recency.meaning: When last/current; do not infer resolution.

frequency.meaning: Reported recurrence within an explicit reference period; no invented numeric conversion.

plan_present.meaning: Whether a plan was explicitly reported or denied.

access.meaning: Access to means as reported, without generating procedural details.

past_behaviour.meaning: Historical self-injury/attempt account, intent and timing.

concepts.question_example: Have you had thoughts about ending your life?
concepts.followup_focus: Use dedicated safety pathway; preserve current versus historical information.
concepts.do_not_infer: Fear of death is not automatically recurrent thoughts of death; self-harm and suicidal intent must be distinguished.
concepts.criterion_review_note: Distinguish recurrent death thoughts/ideation from a specific plan or attempt; fear of dying alone is different. Use the dedicated safety pathway.

concepts.label: Episode timeline
concepts.definition: Period linking symptoms and changes.

onset.meaning: When this particular experience began; preserve approximate wording.

duration.meaning: How long this particular experience has continued, not time needed to perform an activity.

course.meaning: Continuity, fluctuation or change over the relevant period.

intervals.meaning: Earlier periods, recovery and residual symptoms.

concepts.question_example: When did these changes begin?
concepts.followup_focus: Ask only relevant unanswered context; do not conduct every alternative interview.
concepts.do_not_infer: A contextual association is not a confirmed causal explanation.

concepts.label: Functioning and distress
concepts.definition: Reported burden in important life areas.

domain.meaning: Affected area such as work, relationships or self-care.

concepts.question_example: How have these changes affected your daily life?
concepts.followup_focus: Ask only relevant unanswered context; do not conduct every alternative interview.
concepts.do_not_infer: A contextual association is not a confirmed causal explanation.

concepts.label: Activation history
concepts.definition: Possible distinct elevated/overactive periods requiring review.

mood.meaning: Elevated, expansive or irritable mood as reported.

sleep_need.meaning: Sleep need and tiredness, not just sleep hours.

other_changes.meaning: Associated speech, thoughts, confidence or risky behaviour.

concepts.question_example: Have you had a distinct period of unusually increased energy or activity?
concepts.followup_focus: Ask only relevant unanswered context; do not conduct every alternative interview.
concepts.do_not_infer: A contextual association is not a confirmed causal explanation.

concepts.label: Medical context
concepts.definition: Relevant reported medical history and symptoms.

conditions.meaning: Reported conditions; distinguish reported diagnosis from confirmation.

clinician_review.meaning: Known professional assessment or unresolved need.

concepts.question_example: Are there health conditions that might be relevant to these changes?
concepts.followup_focus: Ask only relevant unanswered context; do not conduct every alternative interview.
concepts.do_not_infer: A contextual association is not a confirmed causal explanation.

concepts.label: Medicines and substances
concepts.definition: Relevant treatment/substance exposure account.

dose_use.meaning: Reported amount/use; never recommend a dose.

source_kind.meaning: Medicine, alcohol, other substance or unclear.

concepts.question_example: Have any medicines or substance-use patterns changed around this time?
concepts.followup_focus: Ask only relevant unanswered context; do not conduct every alternative interview.
concepts.do_not_infer: A contextual association is not a confirmed causal explanation.

concepts.label: Psychotic experiences
concepts.definition: Reported experiences requiring specialist interpretation.

kind.meaning: Experience as described, not an automatic diagnosis.

content.meaning: Brief relevant content without affirming beliefs.

reported_mood_congruence.meaning: Professional mood-congruence description if actually supplied; do not invent it.

concepts.question_example: Have you had experiences that other people do not seem to share?
concepts.followup_focus: Ask only relevant unanswered context; do not conduct every alternative interview.
concepts.do_not_infer: A contextual association is not a confirmed causal explanation.

concepts.label: Previous care
concepts.definition: Prior mental-health assessment and care.

response.meaning: Reported benefits, persistence or unwanted effects.

use.meaning: Actual use and barriers as reported.

concepts.question_example: Have you received help for something similar before?
concepts.followup_focus: Ask only relevant unanswered context; do not conduct every alternative interview.
concepts.do_not_infer: A contextual association is not a confirmed causal explanation.

concepts.label: Family history
concepts.definition: Relevant family mood/psychiatric history.

certainty.meaning: How the person knows; unknown remains unknown.

concepts.question_example: Is there relevant mental-health history in your family?
concepts.followup_focus: Ask only relevant unanswered context; do not conduct every alternative interview.
concepts.do_not_infer: A contextual association is not a confirmed causal explanation.

concepts.label: Life context
concepts.definition: Relevant stress, loss, trauma and support.
concepts.question_example: Has anything important been happening around the time these changes began?
concepts.followup_focus: Ask only relevant unanswered context; do not conduct every alternative interview.
concepts.do_not_infer: A contextual association is not a confirmed causal explanation.

concepts.label: Anxious distress
concepts.definition: At least two anxiety features on most episode days; anxious-distress severity is distinct from overall MDD severity.

tension.meaning: Feeling keyed up or tense during the relevant episode.

unusual_restlessness.meaning: Restlessness beyond the person's usual state; separate from observed motor agitation.

worry_affecting_concentration.meaning: Difficulty focusing specifically because of worry.

fear_of_awful_event.meaning: Fear that something awful may happen.

fear_of_losing_control.meaning: Fear of losing control of oneself, as described by the person.

episode_overlap.meaning: Relation to the current or most recent episode.

observer.meaning: Reporter/observer; not a substitute for examination.

concepts.question_example: Ask a focused, neutral question about a relevant feature only.
concepts.followup_focus: The five feature labels refer to tension, restlessness, worry-related concentration difficulty and the two specified fears.
concepts.do_not_infer: Clarify episode overlap and actual experience; do not substitute a generic anxiety score.

concepts.label: Mixed features
concepts.definition: At least three activation features on most episode days, changed from usual and observable; full mania/hypomania changes the bipolar formulation.

elevated_expansive_mood.meaning: Unusually elevated or expansive mood; ordinary happiness is insufficient.

grandiosity.meaning: Unusual inflated self-esteem or grandiose beliefs compared with baseline.

increased_talkativeness.meaning: More talkative than usual or feeling pressure to keep talking.

racing_thoughts.meaning: Reported fast/racing thoughts or rapid shifts between ideas.

increased_energy_activity.meaning: Unusual increase in energy or purposeful activity.

risky_activity.meaning: Unusual involvement in activities with significant potential adverse consequences.

reduced_sleep_need.meaning: Feeling rested despite less sleep, rather than being unable to sleep while tired.

episode_overlap.meaning: Relation to the current or most recent episode.

observer.meaning: Reporter/observer; not a substitute for examination.

concepts.question_example: Ask a focused, neutral question about a relevant feature only.
concepts.followup_focus: Each label means a reported change: expansive mood, inflated self-view, speech, thought speed, energy/activity, consequential risk-taking or less sleep without tiredness.
concepts.do_not_infer: Check exposure effects and professional interpretation. Irritability/agitation alone are not the seven-feature definition.

concepts.label: Melancholic features
concepts.definition: At the episode's worst phase: near-total pleasure loss or little mood response to positive events, plus at least three associated features.

near_total_pleasure_loss.meaning: Almost no enjoyment across almost all activities at the worst episode phase.

low_mood_reactivity.meaning: Little or no temporary mood improvement with usually enjoyable events.

distinct_mood_quality.meaning: Qualitatively distinct despair/despondency/empty mood; severity alone is insufficient.

morning_worsening.meaning: A regular pattern of worse depression in the morning.

early_waking.meaning: Waking earlier than usual; record the actual difference before evaluating the two-hour feature.

marked_motor_change.meaning: Pronounced observable slowing or agitation; retain reporter and uncertainty.

appetite_weight_loss.meaning: Significant appetite/weight loss, with appetite and weight kept distinct.

excessive_guilt.meaning: Reported excessive/inappropriate guilt; proportionality requires clinical interpretation.

episode_overlap.meaning: Relation to the current or most recent episode.

observer.meaning: Reporter/observer; not a substitute for examination.

concepts.question_example: Ask a focused, neutral question about a relevant feature only.
concepts.followup_focus: Associated features are a distinct mood quality, morning worsening, waking at least two hours early, marked motor change, appetite/weight loss and excessive guilt.
concepts.do_not_infer: Mere severity is not distinct mood quality. Preserve observed versus reported motor changes.

concepts.label: Atypical features
concepts.definition: Predominant episode pattern: mood brightening with positive events plus at least two associated features; incompatible melancholic/catatonic criteria must be reviewed.

mood_reactivity.meaning: Mood improvement in response to actual or anticipated positive events.

appetite_weight_gain.meaning: Significant increased appetite or weight, preserving which is reported.

excessive_sleep.meaning: Reported extended sleep compared with usual; retain actual hours/naps and baseline.

leaden_limbs.meaning: A heavy, weighted-down feeling in arms or legs; not objective paralysis.

longstanding_rejection_sensitivity.meaning: Impairing sensitivity to interpersonal rejection that also exists outside mood episodes.

episode_overlap.meaning: Relation to the current or most recent episode.

observer.meaning: Reporter/observer; not a substitute for examination.

concepts.question_example: Ask a focused, neutral question about a relevant feature only.
concepts.followup_focus: Associated features concern increased appetite/weight, excessive sleep, heavy limbs and longstanding impairing sensitivity to rejection beyond the episode.
concepts.do_not_infer: Feeling better briefly does not rule out depression. Atypical is a technical pattern, not any unusual symptom.

concepts.label: Seasonal pattern
concepts.definition: For recurrent MDD: characteristic seasonal onset/remission, a qualifying two-year pattern without nonseasonal episodes, and seasonal predominance across life.

onset_season.meaning: Time of year when actual depressive episodes begin.

remission_season.meaning: Time of year when episodes remit, not merely improve briefly.

two_year_history.meaning: Episode and recovery pattern over the last two years.

nonseasonal_episodes.meaning: Depressive episodes outside the proposed season; include dates.

lifetime_pattern.meaning: Relative lifetime occurrence of seasonal and nonseasonal episodes.

seasonal_stressors.meaning: Season-linked life events that might explain the reported pattern.

episode_overlap.meaning: Relation to the current or most recent episode.

observer.meaning: Reporter/observer; not a substitute for examination.

concepts.question_example: Ask a focused, neutral question about a relevant feature only.
concepts.followup_focus: Record episode dates and recoveries; seasonal work/school stress alone is not this pattern.
concepts.do_not_infer: A single difficult winter does not establish seasonal pattern.

concepts.label: Peripartum/perinatal context
concepts.definition: Formal peripartum onset concerns pregnancy or the first four weeks after delivery; broader perinatal assessment includes the first postpartum year.

pregnancy_delivery_timing.meaning: Pregnancy stage, delivery date or postpartum interval as actually reported.

symptom_onset_timing.meaning: Onset relative to pregnancy and delivery, separately from interview date.

episode_relationship.meaning: Which episode this reproductive context concerns.

parent_infant_functioning.meaning: Reported self-care, caregiving and related functional concerns.

postpartum_psychosis_concerns.meaning: Reported psychotic/confusional/marked activation concerns after delivery requiring urgent professional review.

episode_overlap.meaning: Relation to the current or most recent episode.

observer.meaning: Reporter/observer; not a substitute for examination.

concepts.question_example: Ask a focused, neutral question about a relevant feature only.
concepts.followup_focus: Use actual dates and circumstances, including whether symptoms began before delivery.
concepts.do_not_infer: Later postpartum onset still warrants assessment. Postpartum psychosis requires urgent professional care.

concepts.label: Catatonic signs
concepts.definition: A syndrome requiring at least three recognized signs and professional examination; not equivalent to fatigue or ordinary motor slowing.

stupor.meaning: Markedly reduced movement and responsiveness, requiring clinical observation.

catalepsy.meaning: An examiner-positioned posture maintained against gravity; requires examination.

waxy_flexibility.meaning: Slight even resistance during examiner repositioning; requires examination.

mutism.meaning: Minimal or absent verbal response, requiring appropriate clinical interpretation.

negativism.meaning: Opposition or absent response to instructions/external stimuli in clinical assessment.

posturing.meaning: Spontaneously holding a posture against gravity.

mannerism.meaning: An unusual exaggerated version of an ordinary action.

unprovoked_agitation.meaning: Agitation not influenced by external stimuli in the clinical formulation.

episode_overlap.meaning: Relation to the current or most recent episode.

observer.meaning: Reporter/observer; not a substitute for examination.

concepts.question_example: Ask a focused, neutral question about a relevant feature only.
concepts.followup_focus: Signs cover reduced responsiveness/speech, postural/tone abnormalities, resistance, unusual/repeated movements, agitation and echoing speech/actions. Clinical elicitation is essential.
concepts.do_not_infer: Text silence cannot diagnose mutism or stupor; do not instruct a layperson to perform a physical examination.

finding_status.reported_present: Explicitly described or affirmed in context; not clinical confirmation.
finding_status.conflicting: Accounts for the same subject/period conflict and are retained.

temporal_status.current: Described as relevant to current period.

detail_status.unknown: Relevant but unresolved; no value asserted.
detail_status.not_applicable: Inapplicability is explicitly justified; not equivalent to not asked.

semantic_check_status.supported: Evidence appears to support the claim.
